about: Test data (synthetic: every source is a made-up 'Sample' abstract about made-up models and benchmarks, and every paraphrase is a made-up rewording of it). Labelled source/paraphrase pairs for the paraphrase-fidelity check fidelity(source, paraphrase) (specs/003-judge-fidelity, REQ-033, proposed; the check itself is task T020, a [rules] task, not built yet). Each source has paraphrases of two kinds: 'faithful' ones say the same thing in other words (passive voice, reordered, merged or split sentences, number words, 'percentage points' spelled out) and must pass every check; 'unfaithful' ones carry exactly one defect from the 'defects' list and must fail the one check that 'defectCheck' names for it. 'where' quotes the part of the source the defect concerns (null when the paraphrase adds something the source doesn't have). Validated by test/fidelity-cases.js. Never edit a case to make a checker pass; add a case when a mis-judgement turns up.

sources.title: Sample-Net: a small reasoning model (test data)
sources.text: Sample abstract (test data). We introduce Sample-Net, a 40-million-parameter model trained on 12 synthetic tasks. On a Sample reasoning benchmark, Sample-Net improves accuracy by 4 percentage points over a baseline, averaged over 3 seeds. These results suggest that the method may improve sample efficiency. Limitations: we evaluate only on synthetic data.

sources.title: Sample-Coder: program repair on synthetic bugs (test data)
sources.text: Sample abstract (test data). We present Sample-Coder, a code model evaluated on a Sample program-repair benchmark of 500 synthetic bugs. Sample-Coder fixes 62% of the bugs, up 9 percentage points from the previous Sample baseline. We do not evaluate on real repositories. The gains might not transfer to longer programs.

Real repositories are not evaluated. The gains might not transfer to longer programs.
paraphrases.why: Passive voice; the negation ('not evaluated') and the hedge ('might not') are kept.

sources.title: A Sample reasoning monitor for reward hacking (test data)
sources.text: Sample abstract (test data). We test whether a Sample chain-of-thought monitor detects reward hacking in 200 synthetic episodes. The monitor flags 31 of 47 hacking episodes and raises 5 false alarms. It does not detect hacking when the reasoning is hidden. Our findings indicate that monitoring may help, but only under the conditions we studied.

paraphrases.text: Sample abstract (test data). Whether reward hacking is detected by a Sample chain-of-thought monitor is tested in 200 synthetic episodes. 31 of 47 hacking episodes are flagged by the monitor, and 5 false alarms are raised. Hacking is not detected when the reasoning is hidden. The findings indicate that monitoring may help, but only under the conditions studied.
paraphrases.why: Passive voice throughout; the negation and the scope limit are kept.

paraphrases.text: Sample abstract (test data). We test whether a Sample chain-of-thought monitor detects reward hacking in two hundred synthetic episodes. Our findings indicate that monitoring may help, but only under the conditions we studied.

sources.title: A Sample long-context benchmark (test data)
sources.text: Sample abstract (test data). We release a Sample long-context benchmark with 1,200 synthetic questions over documents of up to 32,000 tokens. Three Sample models score between 41% and 58%. Scores fall by 15 percentage points when the answer appears in the middle of a document. The benchmark covers English text only.

sources.title: Sample-Prune: pruning small language models (test data)
sources.text: Sample abstract (test data). We propose Sample-Prune, a pruning method for small language models. On a Sample summarisation task, Sample-Prune removes 30% of weights while accuracy drops by less than 1 percentage point. We compare against two baselines over 5 seeds. The method may not scale beyond 1 billion parameters, which we leave to future work.

paraphrases.text: Sample abstract (test data). Sample-Prune, a pruning method for small language models, is proposed. On a Sample summarisation task, 30% of weights are removed by Sample-Prune while accuracy drops by less than 1 percentage point. Two baselines are compared against over 5 seeds. Scaling beyond 1 billion parameters may not hold and is left to future work.
paraphrases.why: Passive voice; the bound 'less than 1 percentage point' and the hedge 'may not' are kept.
